title: Indian man living in Canada says parents ask him to return Rs 25 lakh spent on education after money dispute- Moneycontrol.com
summary: A 22-year-old Indian working in Canada says he sends Rs 70,000 monthly to his family, but his parents lock Rs 50,000 into local kametis (chit funds), leaving only Rs 20,000 for household expenses. They frequently ask him for extra top-ups and remind him of about Rs 25 lakh spent on his education, asking him to 'return' it. He sought advice on Reddit; commenters suggested cutting remittances, saving in Canada, or negotiating different saving methods.
content:
Supporting family back home is a goal for many young professionals who move abroad. But what happens when the money they send every month is not used the way they expected? That is the dilemma a 22-year-old Indian working in Canada says he is facing.

Despite sending Rs 70,000 home every month, the young man claimed his parents put most of the money into local committees or chit funds. He said this left them with only Rs 20,000 for household expenses. This situation led to disagreements, with his parents reminding him about the Rs 25 lakh spent on his education. Looking for advice, he shared his situation on Reddit.

The 22-year-old said he is the only earning member of his family and believes the amount he sends every month should be enough to comfortably run the household. However, instead of spending it on regular expenses, he said his parents save most of it through local ‘kametis’.

The user wrote, “My parents put Rs 50,000 of that money every single month into a local ‘kameti’ (committee/chit fund). They put Rs 25k in for my mom, and Rs 25k for my dad. They see it as ‘forced savings,’ but it locks their money up for the year.”

According to him, that decision leaves only Rs 20,000 to cover groceries, utility bills, school fees and other household expenses. The user further added, “Because they’re locking away 50k out of the 70k that I send, they’re left with only 20k to run the entire house… groceries, utilities, my sister's school/admission fees, etc. Now obviously, 20k isn't enough for all this. So almost every month, they turn around and complain to me I’m not sending enough, asking for extra ‘top-ups’ to cover basic bills.”

The repeated requests have started affecting his own finances. The young man said that after paying his own expenses in Canada. “So almost every month, they turn around and complain to me I'm not sending enough, asking for extra ‘top-ups’ to cover basic bills. Just this month, I had to send an extra 25k on top of the 70k, completely throwing off my own personal budget in Canada,” he said.

The Reddit user said he has tried to explain why he believes the arrangement is not practical. The man explained, “I've tried explaining to them that keeping money in a locked committee when you can't cover basic daily needs makes no financial sense. If an emergency happens, that money is stuck.”

Feeling increasingly frustrated, he said he now feels as though he is working only to support their savings plan while putting his own goals on hold. Seeking advice from the online community, he asked whether others had dealt with similar expectations from their parents. He said he has never refused to support his family, but feels the financial pressure has become difficult to manage.

“Has anyone else confronted parents with similar demands? I have not refused to help but when I am already planning on sending 70k every month,” the man asked.

He added that whenever he questioned the arrangement, his parents reminded him that they had spent on his education. He revealed, “They say, “Send all the money back right awayjo tere upar lagaye hain(that we have spent on you),” which is around Rs 25 lakh.”

His post drew many responses, with users offering different opinions. While some felt he should reduce the amount he sends home, others believed his parents were simply trying to secure the family’s future.

I’m 22 y.o male in Canada and supporting my family in India, but I feel like I’m just funding their kametis (those chit-funds) Need advice/vent.byu/Ok-Being1322inpersonalfinanceindia

A user suggested, “Dude you need to cut down on money you're sending them, that is the only way. Tell them expenses are way too high here and ask them to cut down onKametiinvestments by 10-15K.”

Another commenter urged the young man to think about his own financial future as well. The user wrote, “Keep cool, do not worry. Save some money inCanada; even $50 saved will help. Send money to India as per your capacity. It is impossible to manage life in Canada these days. Parents sending their kids abroad should not expect them to pay back Rs 20 lakh or Rs 25 lakh. They should feel that their son or daughter is settled and that future generations will be better off.”

One said, “They’re probably saving for retirement and for your sister’s wedding. They know that once you have your own family, you won’t send as much, so they’re trying to squeeze everything out right now. You have to put your foot down.”

Another user felt the family should complete the current committee cycle before moving future savings into more flexible options. The user explained, “You are 22. What are you talking about marriage and all? Support them until the end of this year, as you can’t get out of the chit system without getting hit. Then next year, say savings should be done in FD or RD.”
